SD-26.question: STU-FX-131a ANGLE rows with hard and soft bounds 0..0: unbounded wrapping angle or literal 0?

sources_checked.what: Generated bindings of the After Effects SDK headers (Apache-2.0/BSD-3/MIT/Zlib): PF_AngleDef has four PF_Fixed fields value, dephault, valid_min, valid_max (16 bytes).
PF_FixedSliderDef field order: value, value_str[32], value_desc[32], valid_min, valid_max, slider_min, slider_max, dephault, precision, display_flags.
AE SDK guide: angle parameters are fixed-point degrees; users can enter multiple revolutions, giving values above 360.
PF_AngleParamSuite1 / PF_GetFloatingPointValueFromAngleDef returns the angle as a float; no range semantics stated.
Community: angle registered with PF_ADD_ANGLE(name, default, id), no range argument (UNVERIFIED secondary source).
OpenFX: kOfxParamDoubleTypeAngle marks a double as an angle; values reach the plug-in in degrees; range defaults not stated on the page (not verified).

Capture decoder: ANGLE shares the FIX_SLIDER branch and reads valid/slider min/max, default and precision at 0x7C-0x93; the union starts at 0x38 (FIX_SLIDER value_in_preset at 0x38, valid_min at 0x7C = 0x38 + 4 + 32 + 32).
Raw captures are working-tree only; installed_exports/ is absent on this machine (checked kernel and offline-green-room), so a re-decode was not possible.

All 78 ANGLE rows surveyed: 50 carry numeric bounds from pard records (32 all-zero, 18 impossible or implausible pairs such as 0..-1.5e-05, 1..32000, 0.003906..0.496094), 22 PresetEffects.xml rows and 6 layer-style rows carry `--` bounds.

Folio reads Twirl Angle and Hue/Saturation hues as unbounded (no-range encoding), but keeps Directional Blur Direction soft 0..7936 (declared_soft_only) and Glow Color Phase hard 0.003906..0.496094 degrees.

findings: PF_AngleDef is 16 bytes: value at union offset 0, default at +4, valid_min at +8, valid_max at +12; with the union at record offset 0x38 these sit at 0x38, 0x3C, 0x40, 0x44.

ae_common.decode_pard reads ANGLE records with the FIX_SLIDER layout (valid_min 0x7C, valid_max 0x80, slider_min 0x84, slider_max 0x88, default 0x8C, precision 0x90). Those offsets lie 0x34+ bytes past the end of PF_AngleDef, so every numeric bound, default and precision cell of a pard-origin ANGLE row is unrelated record bytes, not a declaration.

This explains the pattern in the tables: 32 rows read 0..0 (zeroed padding) and 18 rows read impossible values (max below min, 1..32000 on a direction, a 0.003906..0.496094 degree hard range on Glow Color Phase, 0..255 with default 127.5 on Drop Shadow Direction).
Neither literal reading of 0..0 is right: it is neither a declared unbounded marker nor a declared lock to 0. It is absence of a decoded declaration, which [STU-FX-106] names unbounded_in_source.

The AE SDK does carry valid_min/valid_max inside PF_AngleDef, so some effects may declare a real angle range; whether shipped effects set it is UNVERIFIED until the captures are re-decoded at 0x40/0x44 (captures are absent on this machine).

The ANGLE default and precision cells are equally unproven; the defaults recorded for pard rows are provisional (UNVERIFIED). Defaults on the 22 PresetEffects.xml rows were parsed from XML and are unaffected.

Field: AE stores angles as signed fixed-point degrees with whole revolutions (2x+0 is 720), and OpenFX passes angles in degrees; neither reduces the stored value modulo 360. Folio's own test stores Twirl Angle -720.
Product defect found: folio Glow Color Phase rejects any phase above 0.496094 degrees, and Directional Blur Direction presents a 0..7936 soft range; both come from the misread bytes.
SD-26.field_expectation: Effect SDKs declare an angle by value and default; a range is optional and usually absent. Hosts store the full signed degree value including extra revolutions and present it as revolutions plus remainder; they do not clamp an angle that declares no range.
SD-26.recommendation: Read every pard-origin ANGLE row as unbounded_in_source (four bounds null, shown as `--`), keep its default and precision as provisional UNVERIFIED values pending a re-decode at the angle offsets, store full signed degrees including revolutions, and fix the decoder (governance tool) so a later capture run reads 0x3C/0x40/0x44.

SD-27.question: Foam Viscosity, Wave World Damping and Wave Speed declare no unit: which unit or explicit dimensionless token?

sources_checked.what: Adobe help for Foam / Wave World: BLOCKED (HTTP 403 to WebFetch).
After Effects user manual mirror (via search snippets): Wave Speed = how fast waves travel from their start; Damping = how quickly the liquid absorbs wave energy; no unit stated.
Foam Physics controls (via search snippets): Viscosity raises resistance so bubbles slow and stop; Universe Size is relative to the layer; no unit stated.
FIX_SLIDER carries only display_flags (percent, pixel) besides range/default/precision: the SDK has no unit field.
OpenFX kOfxParamDoubleTypePlain: an uninterpreted number the user sees as passed; kOfxParamDoubleTypeScale for 0..1 factors.
Units come only from DISPLAY_PERCENT / DISPLAY_PIXEL flags (and ANGLE = degrees); a FIX_SLIDER without those flags has no recoverable unit.
StudioUnitToken already has `unitless`; a parameter whose source declares no unit carries `unitless`.
Folio maps the source `--` to Unitless.
Engine scalars carry Studio-authored units: viscosity 1/s, damping 1/s, wave_speed cells/s.

findings: The effect SDK has no unit field for sliders; the only unit-like data is the percent/pixel display flags, which these rows do not set. The vendor help describes all three controls qualitatively with no unit.
The spec already answers the unit: [STU-FX-108] makes an undeclared source unit `unitless`. The gap is a reading conflict in [STU-FX-131a], whose `--` text says Studio declares nothing.
Other systems type such sliders as plain uninterpreted numbers (OpenFX DoubleTypePlain); none invents a physical unit.

The real gap is the engine mapping: the record rows are unitless coefficients (Viscosity 0..4, Damping 0..1, Wave Speed 0.01..10), while the engine uses 1/s and cells/s. Matching them needs a declared conversion, and keeping both as editable scalars gives two controls for one quantity.

Adjacent (not edited): Wave World row 24 is named `Pre-roll (seconds)` but its unit cell is `--`; the unit sits in the recovered name. The spec owner can decide whether a unit carried by the recovered name counts as declared.
SD-27.field_expectation: Unitless sliders are stored as plain numbers on the effect's own scale; hosts do not attach a physical unit that the source does not declare.
SD-27.recommendation: Declare the three rows `unitless` explicitly (`--` in a numeric row's unit column is the STU-FX-108 `unitless` token); make the recovered row the single stored value and have the engine read it through one Studio-declared, documented scale per row (UNVERIFIED until an oracle confirms), instead of keeping a second editable studio_declared engine scalar for the same quantity.

SD-29.question: Stream sentinels for markers, column/frame/page/odd-page/even-page breaks and flush space.

sources_checked.what: InDesign scripting: distinct enumerators AUTO_PAGE_NUMBER, NEXT_PAGE_NUMBER, PREVIOUS_PAGE_NUMBER, SECTION_MARKER, FOOTNOTE_SYMBOL, COLUMN_BREAK, FRAME_BREAK, PAGE_BREAK, ODD_PAGE_BREAK, EVEN_PAGE_BREAK, FORCED_LINE_BREAK, FLUSH_SPACE, FIXED_WIDTH_NONBREAKING_SPACE, NONBREAKING_SPACE and the other spaces.
Community: column and frame breaks share the carriage-return code of a paragraph end inside InDesign, distinguished by a break attribute (secondary source).
IDML reader documentation: page number is processing instruction ACE 18, next/previous via a PageNumberType attribute on the range; section marker is ACE 19.

IDML:
ends a paragraph; U+2028 is a forced line break inside Content; U+2029 is not written by InDesign.
Practitioner sheet (via search snippet; direct fetch 404): ParagraphBreakType NextFrame / NextPage / NextOddPage / NextEvenPage on the break's range (UNVERIFIED).
Practitioner note: character-level ParagraphBreakType always forces a break, while paragraph-level StartParagraph does not advance if already at the start (UNVERIFIED).
InDesign GREP codes: ~M column, ~R frame, ~P page, ~L odd page, ~E even page, ~x section marker, ~N/~X/~V page numbers, ~f flush space: each break and marker is searchable as its own character.
Adobe hidden-character glossary (search snippet): flush space fills the last line of justified text. Direct fetch BLOCKED (403) for helpx pages.
OOXML w:br types: page, column, textWrapping (character-level); odd/even page exist only as section break types.
ODF: fo:break-before / fo:break-after are paragraph properties (auto, column, page); even-page and odd-page added for ODF 1.4.
RTF 1.6: \line forced line break; \sbkcol/\sbkpage/\sbkodd/\sbkeven section breaks.

Unicode FAQ: 66 noncharacters including U+FDD0..U+FDEF, intended for internal use (placeholders, sentinels), valid in strings since Corrigendum #9; private-use characters are for interchange and fonts map them.
U+2001 EM QUAD canonically decomposes to U+2003 (NFC maps it to U+2003); U+FDD0 is Cn with no decomposition; U+FFFC is So.
Flush space is an InDesign-specific space with no Unicode equivalent (secondary source).
UTF-8 stream with independent character-range and paragraph partitions; start_paragraph is a six-value paragraph attribute; no stream sentinel scheme exists anywhere in the module.
Anchored items are typed records keyed by anchor_byte, 'inline: the start of its placeholder character', with U+FFFC in tests; footnotes name the host byte of their reference.

Lane keeps 9 markers, 5 breaks and flush space as StreamForm::Pending; real members use Unicode scalars (U+2028 forced line break, U+2029 paragraph return, U+2002..U+200A spaces, U+00A0/U+202F non-breaking spaces).

findings: Layout text models use two encodings side by side. Character level: InDesign has one enumerator per break and per marker, GREP finds each as its own character, OOXML writes w:br page/column, RTF \page/\line. Attribute level: inside InDesign, column/frame breaks share the paragraph-end code with a break attribute; IDML writes ACE 18 plus a PageNumberType attribute for current/next/previous page, and Br plus a ParagraphBreakType attribute for breaks; ODF stores breaks as paragraph properties; OOXML and RTF store odd/even page only as section properties.

Studio already has the paragraph-level counterpart (STU-TYP-186 start_paragraph, six values). STU-TYP-207 and MT-31007 ('distinct stream sentinels') call for character-level members, so each break and marker needs its own stream form.

An attribute on the terminating character is fragile in a model whose character ranges and paragraphs are independent partitions: range edits and overrides can split or drop it. One sentinel per member is searchable, survives copy/paste and gives one stream character per inserted catalog member, as the InDesign scripting and GREP surfaces present it.

Unicode noncharacters U+FDD0..U+FDEF are the standard internal-sentinel block: never assigned, not mapped by fonts, unchanged by normalization, valid in UTF-8 and Rust char. Private use (U+E000..U+F8FF) collides with icon fonts and foreign text.

Flush space must not be U+2001: U+2001 canonically decomposes to U+2003 EM SPACE, so normalization (search, import, clipboard) would silently turn flush space into an em space; Unicode also defines U+2001 as a fixed em quad, not a slack-absorbing space. InDesign's own internal code point for flush space is UNVERIFIED.

U+FFFC OBJECT REPLACEMENT CHARACTER is the Unicode placeholder for an embedded object and is what folio's anchored items already sit on; reusing it for the anchored-object marker avoids a second convention.
Breaks end their paragraph in InDesign (shared paragraph-end code), so a break sentinel must act as a paragraph terminator in the STU-TYP-110 partition.
SD-29.field_expectation: Breaks and page-number/section markers are distinct addressable text elements, stored either as distinct control characters or as a paragraph-end/marker character plus a type attribute; odd/even page breaks degrade to section properties in word-processor formats; flush space is an application-specific space without a Unicode equivalent.
SD-29.recommendation: Assign Unicode noncharacters U+FDD0..U+FDDD to the 14 members without a Unicode character (6 markers, cross-reference and index markers, 5 breaks, flush space), reuse U+FFFC for the anchored-object marker, reserve U+FDDE..U+FDEF, make break sentinels paragraph terminators, keep markers' targets in typed byte-keyed records, and define the import/export mappings (IDML ACE 18/19 + PageNumberType, Br + ParagraphBreakType, OOXML w:br and section breaks, ODF fo:break-before to start_paragraph).

assignment.stored_as: U+FFFC OBJECT REPLACEMENT CHARACTER (the placeholder at the anchored item's story byte)

SD-29.paragraph_attribute_note: Field formats that store these as attributes: IDML (PageNumberType on the ACE 18 range; ParagraphBreakType on the Br range), ODF (fo:break-before/after on the paragraph), OOXML/RTF (odd/even page only as section breaks). Studio keeps the paragraph-level form as STU-TYP-186 start_paragraph and maps ODF paragraph breaks there; IDML character-level breaks map to the sentinels.

SD-29: stream encoding. A member that is a real Unicode character is stored as that scalar; forced
line break is U+2028 and paragraph return is U+2029. A member with no Unicode character carrying
its meaning is stored as one Studio stream sentinel from the Unicode noncharacter block
U+FDD0..U+FDEF, which Unicode reserves for internal use, which fonts do not map, and which no
normalization form changes. Private-use code points are NOT used, because fonts and foreign text
carry them legitimately. The assignment below is stable; U+FDDE..U+FDEF are reserved for later
Studio sentinels and MUST NOT be given another meaning.

*Derivation: contract table carried into this clause's own microtask as acceptance criteria; yields no microtask of its own.*

| Member | Catalog | Stored as |
|---|---|---|
| current page number | Markers | U+FDD0 |
| next page number | Markers | U+FDD1 |
| previous page number | Markers | U+FDD2 |
| section marker | Markers | U+FDD3 |
| footnote reference | Markers | U+FDD4 |
| endnote reference | Markers | U+FDD5 |
| anchored-object marker | Markers | U+FFFC OBJECT REPLACEMENT CHARACTER (the placeholder at the anchored item's story byte) |
| cross-reference marker | Markers | U+FDD6 |
| index marker | Markers | U+FDD7 |
| column break | Break characters | U+FDD8 |
| frame break | Break characters | U+FDD9 |
| page break | Break characters | U+FDDA |
| odd-page break | Break characters | U+FDDB |
| even-page break | Break characters | U+FDDC |
| flush space | White-space characters | U+FDDD |

A marker sentinel carries no text: its kind, target and options live in a typed record keyed by the
sentinel's story byte, composition shows the resolved value without rewriting the stream, and an
unresolved marker shows an explicit unresolved state, never a guessed value. Each break sentinel
ends its paragraph exactly as U+2029 does, so the paragraph partition of [STU-TYP-110] treats it as
a terminator, and its flow target applies after it; it is distinct from the paragraph attribute
`start_paragraph` of [STU-TYP-186], which places a paragraph's start and is stored on the paragraph.
Flush space is a sentinel and not U+2001 EM QUAD, because U+2001 canonically decomposes to U+2003
EM SPACE and would become an em space under normalization. On import, a code point in
U+FDD0..U+FDEF arriving in foreign text is never read as a sentinel: it is replaced and the loss
reported. A source that stores a page-number marker as one marker plus a current/next/previous
attribute, or a break as a paragraph end plus a break-type attribute, maps to the matching
sentinel. On export, a target with no equivalent reports the loss: plain text receives the
resolved marker value, U+2029 for a break and U+0020 for flush space, and a target whose odd-page
and even-page breaks exist only as section properties receives them there.

ordered map from a four-character OpenType feature tag to a value (a boolean for a binary feature,
an unsigned integer for an alternate index). Studio MUST carry a registry of at least the 229
feature tags observed in the captured design-tool feature union, and MUST accept any well-formed
four-character tag not in the registry, storing and applying it. Studio MUST NOT ship a closed
feature list.

ordered map from a four-character OpenType feature tag to a value (a boolean for a binary feature,
an unsigned integer for an alternate index). Studio MUST carry a registry of at least the 229
feature tags observed in the captured design-tool feature union, and MUST accept any well-formed
four-character tag not in the registry, storing and applying it. Studio MUST NOT ship a closed
feature list.

SD-30: the registry is the table below, 245 tags: the 243 feature tags registered in OpenType 1.9.1
(126 registry rows; `cv01`-`cv99` and `ss01`-`ss20` each count every member; `hngl` and `opbd`
are registered but deprecated) plus the two tags `abrv` and `just` that the captured union carries
and the registry does not. The captured union is the 229-tag `OpenTypeFeature` set of the
design-tool plugin API; it omits 16 registered tags (`abvf`, `apkn`, `c2sc`, `chws`, `frac`,
`jalt`, `lnum`, `mset`, `onum`, `pnum`, `smcp`, `subs`, `sups`, `tnum`, `vapk`, `vchw`), which the
registry still carries. A deprecated tag is stored and applied like any other and is not offered
for new authoring. The registry is not closed: any well-formed tag outside it is still accepted.
